subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should ClickClack permanently use a fixed 30-second completion deadline for every non-multipart REST call while leaving multipart uploads unbounded, including outbound writes whose remote commit may be ambiguous after timeout?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish that the deadline works, but code evidence cannot determine the intended ClickClack service budget, upload exception, or retry semantics for a write that may already have committed.

options.title: Approve current policy
options.body: Keep the fixed 30-second JSON REST deadline and multipart exception, accepting ambiguous remote outcomes for timed-out writes.

options.title: Retune by operation
options.body: Use owner-chosen deadlines or idempotency-aware handling that distinguishes reads, activity writes, message writes, and uploads.

options.title: Wait for API contract
options.body: Pause until ClickClack documents request-duration and committed-write retry guarantees.

recommendation.title: Approve current policy
recommendation.body: Keep the fixed 30-second JSON REST deadline and multipart exception, accepting ambiguous remote outcomes for timed-out writes.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history ties this person most directly to the ClickClack client and inbound/outbound contract changed by the PR.
